thread: sam.k: Hey team - customer hitting streaming cutoff ~30s into response when they include our billing header. Happens reliably for them. Request id: req_6f4b2a9c. Logs show a 200 then TCP close from client side. Example server log snippet: `stream_start req=req_6f4b2a9c`, `stream_chunk token=...`, `client_closed req=req_6f4b2a9c at 30.2s` Tara.eng: Thanks, can you attach the minimal curl you used? Need exact headers (including billing header) + whether they're using cookies vs signed cookies. Also include curl -v output if possible. :mag: sam.k: i've got a reproduction from customer. they asked to keep API key redacted but reproduced headers. paste below. note they use a cookie and X-Billing-Org header with a colon in value (weird): ``` curl -N -v \ -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ -H "X-Billing-Org: acct:team-42" \ -H "Cookie: session=eyJhbGci..." \ https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-stream-v2 ``` Curl -v shows: `* Connected to api.redwood.example` then SSE data lines for ~30s then `* Closed` from client. They say same happens for multiple regions. mike.sre: interesting. two quick hypotheses: 1) some proxies or libcurl treat ':' in header values oddly (splits into header name?) 2) chunk parsing gets tripped when cookie contains `=` and long base64. Let's try a minimal isolated repro with no cookie to see if billing header alone triggers it. Also ask them to try `--no-buffer` and `--raw`. Tara.eng: i'll try locally. quick follow steps for the customer to collect a debug bundle if the next repro fails: 1) run the curl with `-vvv --no-buffer` and capture stdout/stderr to a file, 2) include the exact request_id they see, 3) tcpdump of the connection (pcap) if possible, 4) browser repro (fetch) snippet if they used browser. ask to redact API key. support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4527 for streaming cutoff investigation (linked to req_6f4b2a9c). Tara.eng: I reproduced a similar cut locally when I add an extra CRLF after a comment in the cookie header string (weird client-side lib behavior). Here's a minimal curl I used to validate server behavior (no cookie): ``` # minimal streaming repro without cookie curl -N --no-buffer -v \ -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ -H "X-Billing-Org: acct-team-42" \ https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-stream-v2 ``` This stayed open for >2m with continuous chunks. So server side stream looks OK when cookie removed and billing header value sanitized (no colon). mike.sre: good. next ask the customer to try the same minimal repro but with `--header "X-Billing-Org: acct:team-42"` (exact value) AND `--no-buffer --raw -vvv` and paste the full verbose log. If they still hit cutoff, we want the pcap and their curl version. Also ask them to try `--http1.1` vs `--http2` (some libs switch to HTTP/2 which may affect streaming). sam.k: forwarding steps now. customer said they can run tcpdump and will redact keys. i'll post back the verbose curl when they reply. :thumbsup: Tara.eng: also note for internal triage: add a quick unit check in the front-proxy that rejects header values with unescaped colons in X-Billing-Org for streaming routes (temporary guard) while we root cause client parsing behavior. I'll open a PR if we get reproducible trace. mike.sre: thanks. if reproducer comes back, i'll take packet traces and confirm whether TLS close was sent by server or client. If client, we can suggest an SDK workaround (strip cookie or base64-encode differently). sam.k: updated: customer uploaded curl -vvv log and pcap link (private). log shows `* Received EOF` after last SSE comment line and ` 0` nothing else. attaching in ticket. will follow up when they finish tcpdump upload.
